newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM output up, earnings down in 1996.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM output up, earnings down in 1996.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) copper and cobalt production rose in 1996 from 1995, but the company's earnings dropped as a result of reduced exports and falling metal prices, Finance Minister Ronald Penza said.
He said copper production increased to 313,003 tonnes in 1996 from 307,558 tonnes. Cobalt production increased to 4,829 tonnes from 2,866 tonnes the previous year.

"Production for the metal sector would have been higher had it not been for a number of factors, including a fire accident at the Mufulira sector which led to a loss of output," Penza told parliament.
ZCCM earnings, however, declined to a low of $567.7 million, largely as a result of reduced copper exports, which dropped to 327,473 tonnes from 341,443 tonnes in 1995.
Penza said falling metal prices between June and October 1996 also contributed to the reduced earnings.
However, cobalt exports increased by 66 percent to 3,866 tonnes boosting export earnings by 42.2 percent to $192.5 million.
Penza said multinational mining houses spent between $25 and $30 million in exploration work during the year.
"Significant exploration results were obtained in the Copperbelt, North-Western and Central Provinces," he said.

Dunrobin Mining a subsidiary of Reunion Mining Plc, completed feasibility studies and started the construction of a medium-scale gold production facility at Dunrobin mine in the central Mumbwa district.

Penza said the privatisation of ZCCM, which kicked off with the acquisation of 80 percent intrest in Kansanshi copper mine by Cyprus Amax Minerals Company in January, would gather momentum during the year.
"Bids for the other packages of ZCCM are due at the end of February this year. The sales are expected to be substantially completed during the third quarter of 1997," Penza said.

He said a memorandum of understanding was expected to be signed between Zambia and a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa on the development of Konkola Deep mine this month, with other transanctions being signed in the third quarter o the year.
The government had also accepted a proposal from Avmin Ltd for the exploration, evaluation and development of Konkola North.
"An option agreement is due to be signed in February under which Avmin Ltd will conduct additional drilling and a pre-feasibility study over the next 24 months," Penza said.
